chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a woman who fell ill during the month of Ramadan, or menstruated, or travelled, and then died before the end of the month of Ramadan. Does her fasting have to be made up on her behalf? He said: As for menstruation and illness, no; and as for travel, yes.

key_terms.رَمَضَانُ: The month of Ramadan, during which fasting is obligatory
key_terms.يُقْضَى: To make up (for missed obligatory acts)

ai.seo_question: Does a woman who dies during Ramadan need to have her missed fasts made up if she was menstruating or ill versus traveling?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distinction between temporary impediments that incur a debt of fasting and those that do not, ruling that menstruation and illness exempt a woman from makeup fasting upon death, whereas travel requires it. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic view that menstruation is a natural state of exemption rather than a temporary excuse requiring restitution, while travel is a temporary impediment to the obligation. The hadith underscores the principle that the obligation to make up fasts is tied to the nature of the excuse and the ability to fulfill the duty if one had survived.
